why: Tried all three refutation axes and none holds. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md (1679 lines) carries the quoted sentence word-for-word at :1437, opening the section '### Memory index is over its read limit'. Read the WHOLE line — it is three sentences and the other two REINFORCE rather than reverse: 'The write succeeded, but only the first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, load at the start of a session, so everything past the limit is dropped each time the index is read. Before v2.1.210, an over-limit index was silently truncated on the next load with no write-time signal.' The surrounding block adds the literal error text (:1440, naming line count and the 'Rewrite it to under 140 lines' remedy), a {/* min-version: 2.1.211 */} refinement that frontmatter and block-level HTML comments are stripped before measurement, 'Claude Code delivers the error to Claude after the write rather than printing it as a banner', and 'When Claude's write brings the file near a limit without crossing it, Claude Code returns a milder reminder to compact the index instead of this error.' :101 lists the error in the top-level index table. The page is row 102 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv ('errors	Error reference'), so it is a valid Claude contract citation, not a Codex or MCP page. (2) CITED CODE says what was claimed. memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-33 is readMemoryFile doing `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — a silent slice, no signal. remember.ts:39-49 is appendMemory: read existing, formatMemoryFile, write temp, rename, chmod — and :90-91 is `appendMemory(filePath, memory); return successResponse(`Saved memory to ${filePath}`);`. No measurement, no error, no reminder. (3) CONSEQUENCE verified separately from the identifier, one layer up and one layer down, including the sibling-subsystem trap. UP: `remember` is live and model-reachable (tool-defs.ts:981, safeMode 'block'). DOWN/SIBLING: there is a SECOND writer on a different subsystem — appendMemoryFile (memory-store.ts:122-132), reached by the renderer RPC path ChatDisplay.tsx:1557 -> dto.ts:519 `{type:'appendMemory'}` -> sessions.ts:564 -> :80 — and it has no post-write check either, so naming only the tool path understates it. Absence positively controlled with `rg -na` (NUL-byte-safe) for 'over its|read limit|left the memory|rewrite it to under|near a limit' across packages/ and apps/: zero memory-related hits, so neither the hard error nor the documented milder near-limit reminder exists. No byte cap exists anywhere on the memory path: the only *_MAX_BYTES in the subsystem is AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256*1024 (memory-cleanup.ts:33), a skip-guard in the scheduled dream pass (:125 leaves oversized files unchanged), not a 25KB load or write limit. No frontmatter or block-level HTML-comment exclusion: only the auto-marker `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` is stripped (stripAutoMemoryMarkers, memory-store.ts:159-163), and in the legacy path that strip happens in mergeMemoryContents AFTER the 200-line slice. NOT an owner decision: 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches memory limits. NOT a deliberate product difference either: this fork has a real auto-memory subsystem (remember tool + marker + scheduled cleanup), so the de-brand, the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows and the corporate gateway are all irrelevant here. Note for the collector: this substantially duplicates f103 (same defect cited from memory.md:386) and is adjacent to f092/f098/f104 (the missing 25KB load cap) — one fix closes all of them.
correctedState: Confirmed, with one clause of the submitted wording corrected and two scope additions. CORRECTION: 'we DO silently truncate at load' is true only on the LEGACY composer. prompts/system.ts:453-455 calls loadMemoryPromptBlock — the sole route to readMemoryFile's 200-line slice — only when `capabilityContextPinned` is false. On the live capability-runtime path, composePinnedCapabilityContext (base-agent.ts:975-1015) reads each memory layer with `await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)`, which returns the whole file; the only content ever removed there is `@import` lines (:1003-1007) and `paths:`-rule bodies. So the fork has TWO memory paths and NEITHER matches the doc: the legacy one truncates at 200 lines with no write-time signal (the pre-v2.1.210 defect the page describes), and the live one applies no cap at all. ADDITION 1: the missing write-time measurement covers BOTH writers, not just the tool — appendMemory (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:39-49, returning only `Saved memory to <path>` at :91) and appendMemoryFile (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:122-132), the latter reached by the renderer RPC at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:80. ADDITION 2: the documented MILDER near-limit reminder is missing too, not only the hard error. Otherwise as claimed: no 25KB byte limit anywhere (AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256*1024 at memory-cleanup.ts:33 is a cleanup skip-guard, not a load or write cap), and no frontmatter / block-level HTML-comment exclusion from the measurement — only the `<!-- nessy:auto:DATE -->` marker is stripped, and in the legacy path after the slice.
